verdicts.question: Who are the pre-processors within about 150 km of Bengaluru that turn yard bales and lots into factory feedstock (PET flake/washing lines, plastic reprocessors, cable granulators, tyre shredders/crumb/pyrolysis, C&D plants, ELV/RVSFs, e-waste dismantlers, used-oil re-refiners, foundry-sand reclaimers)? Give counts, names, capacities and clusters.
verdicts.problems: Source check could not be run on this machine: the session's WebSearch budget is exhausted (200/200) and every page fetch is refused by the proxy (CONNECT 403), so none of the 28 cited sources was seen in a snippet today; under the brief's rule an unverified key claim defaults to holds=false, and the specific problems below were found by internal checks. (1) Internal contradiction: the answer says Chaitra Civil Ventures won a 'Rs 1,052-crore, 15-year' debris contract, but the cited Deccan Herald headline in its own source list says 'Rs 1,714-crore'; one of the two numbers is wrong and neither is snippet-confirmed. (2) Arithmetic: '1,000 TPD ... ran at about 10% (around 200 t/day)' does not add up; 10% of 1,000 is 100 t/day. (3) Weak or second-hand sources for headline counts: the named plastic units and capacities come from a Scribd re-upload of a 2022 CPCB list, the '143 units / 2.10 lakh t/yr' figure from a coaching-site page (nammakpsc.com) with no date, and Cerebra's '90,000 t/yr' from a competitor's blog; none is an official page and none was confirmed. (4) Ash Recyclers at '52,722 MT/yr' is an outlier an order of magnitude above every other named dismantler and is not confirmed by snippet; treat as suspect until the CPCB list is opened. (5) Currency: the KSPCB e-waste counts (27/42/24/14), the Quint tyre-pyrolysis counts (34/12/3/19/8), the 2019 and 2023 CPCB e-waste lists and the 2017 C&D paper are all undated or years old; the answer does not say which are still current in 2026, and the Bengaluru C&D generation figure of 2,000-2,500 t/day is from an older Deccan Herald piece. From background knowledge (not snippet-confirmed): Cerebra Integrated Technologies was the subject of SEBI action in 2023 over its accounts, so its Narasapura e-waste unit's operating status needs a phone check before it is seeded as a buyer. (6) Fit with the founder's refined chain: the answer files lead smelters, used-oil re-refiners and tyre-pyrolysis plants under 'pre-processor', but the founder's role table puts remelting, re-refining and chemical recovery under 'recycler/reprocessor' (S7 output) and reserves 'pre-processor' for shredding, washing, drying, granulation, stripping and depollution (S3 to S4-S6). Battery breakers, tyre shredders/crumb lines, PET wash lines, cable granulators, e-waste dismantlers, RVSFs and C&D crushers are pre-processors; smelters, re-refiners and pyrolysis units are recyclers. Most Karnataka units are integrated (they do both), so each seeded business needs a per-process flag rather than a single role. The answer also gives no main-output/by-product/residual structure for any unit, which the refined model needs for every processing record.
verdicts.correction: Same named units, with these changes. Report the Chaitra Civil Ventures contract value as 'Rs 1,714 crore per the Deccan Herald headline (the Rs 1,052-crore figure is unsupported); confirm on the BBMP/BSWML tender page'. Say 'Rock Crystals is rated 1,000 TPD and in 2017 ran at roughly 10%, about 100 t/day' (drop 'around 200'). Mark the plastics count, the '143 units / 2.10 lakh t/yr' figure, Ash Recyclers' 52,722 MT/yr and Cerebra's 90,000 t/yr as unverified secondary-source figures, and add a check on Cerebra's current operating status before onboarding. Re-tag units by the state transition they perform so they fit the founder's chain: pre-processors (S3 to S4-S6) = E-Parisaraa, Eco-E-Waste, Nobel Technology and the other KSPCB dismantlers; Mahindra CERO RVSF (S1 to S4 stripped fractions plus depollution); Rock Crystals, Kannur and Jigani C&D crushers (S4 aggregate); tyre shredder/crumb lines; PET wash lines (S5/S6 flake); cable granulators. Recyclers (S7) = Sri Ponni, Veera Narayana, Evershine, Sri Saraswathi and Mekala lead smelters; Lube Tech, Balaji, Arun, Nakoda and Century used-oil re-refiners; the 12 compliant tyre-pyrolysis units; plastic granule reprocessors such as Keerthana, Anwar, RNZ, Prem and Ishvarya. Seed each business with a list of processes it runs, each carrying main output, saleable by-products and residual (e.g., PET wash line: flake main; PP/HDPE caps and labels by-product; sludge and fines residual to TSDF), rather than one role. Keep the clusters (Peenya; Bommasandra-Attibele-Veerasandra-Jigani; Dobaspet/Nelamangala; Kumbalagodu; Devanahalli-Chikkajala-Kannur; Hoskote) as stated but labelled 'from addresses in undated lists, not confirmed today'. Status stays 'partly'; every count is an open item until the CPCB EPR plastic-portal PWP list, the KSPCB e-waste list, the CPCB tyre portal and the CPCB lead-acid list can be opened.

verdicts.question: What do these pre-processors pay yards for bales and lots, what do they sell outputs for, and what lot sizes, payment terms, freight, quality deductions and sourcing rules apply?
verdicts.problems: No cited source could be checked today (WebSearch budget exhausted, page fetches refused with proxy 403), so none of the 31 marketplace and index figures is snippet-confirmed; the answer itself concedes almost all prices are undated listings and none is Bengaluru-specific. Internal checks found: (1) 'No India price for intact lead-acid batteries per kg was found' is contradicted by the repo's own market research, which cites scraprates.in (Bangalore) at Rs 70-90/kg for batteries; that is a door/L1-L2 figure, but it should be stated and the L3 smelter buy price left open, not 'none found'. (2) Tyre prices conflict with prior repo research: this answer gives whole tyres Rs 12-22/kg from IndiaMART city listings, while market.md (Reporters' Collective) has domestic waste tyres at Rs 20-25/kg; the answer should show both and the reason (registered pyrolysis buyers vs traders). (3) Unreconciled numbers: the ChemAnalyst r-HDPE index of USD 1,238/t (about Rs 105/kg at Rs 85/USD) is roughly 40% above the 'reprocessed HDPE granules Rs 65-77/kg' the answer recommends; the IMARC rPET figure (USD 763/t, about Rs 65/kg) is a flake price yet sits in the granule sentence; the Delhi UBC quote of Rs 194-238/kg is at or above the primary aluminium price and is almost certainly a mislabelled listing, not evidence of a 'swing'. (4) Stale mix: recycled-aggregate prices (Rs 350-400/t) and the Rs 134/t tipping fee are from a 2017 paper but are set against August 2026 M-sand and crushed-stone prices with no inflation caveat. (5) APR bale-spec details ('truckload of roughly 16 t', 'moisture over 4% deducted at tested-percent minus 2%') are not confirmed by any snippet and read as paraphrase; the claim that Indian buyers 'apply these informally' has no source. (6) Newer rules missed on payment terms: since 10 Oct 2024 metal scrap bought from unregistered sellers is under GST reverse charge (Notification 06/2024-CT(Rate)) and registered buyers deduct 2% GST TDS on metal-scrap contracts over Rs 2.5 lakh (Notification 25/2024-CT); Budget 2026-27 proposed income-tax TCS on scrap at 2% from 1 Apr 2026 (repo legal.md, rate to confirm). These change net cash to a yard on HMS, UBC and copper lots and belong in 'payment terms', not a one-line CA referral. (7) Fit with the refined chain: the founder's L3 row reads 'pre-processor/recycler -> yard, processed feedstock, flake/washed-flake/granule price', which is ambiguous between the bale the pre-processor buys and the feedstock it sells; the answer labels bale buy prices 'L3' and outputs 'L3/L4' without resolving this. Under the refined model every trade should carry the material state (S3 bale bought; S5/S6 flake or S7 granule sold) and every processing record should log yield, by-product lots (caps/labels, steel wire, fibre) and residual lots (sludge, fines) with their own prices or disposal costs; the answer's 'buyer deduction field' captures only part of this.
verdicts.correction: Keep the ranges as unverified defaults, with these fixes: lead-acid batteries: door price Rs 70-90/kg (scraprates.in Bangalore, from repo market.md); smelter buy price at L3 open. Tyres: Rs 12-25/kg (trader listings Rs 12-22; registered pyrolysis buyers Rs 20-25 per Reporters' Collective). HDPE granules: listings Rs 65-77/kg vs index about Rs 105/kg (USD 1,238/t); use Rs 65-90/kg as the default band and mark the gap as an open item by grade (natural vs mixed colour). rPET: flake index USD 763/t (about Rs 65/kg) supports hot-washed flake at Rs 55-65/kg; granules Rs 75-90/kg remain listing-based. Drop the Delhi UBC Rs 194-238/kg figure; keep UBC Rs 95-120/kg. Recycled aggregate: 2017 figure of Rs 350-400/t should be uplifted and re-quoted from Rock Crystals or BSWML; do not compare directly with Aug 2026 stone prices. Bale-spec deduction rules: cite as 'APR PET bale spec (rules to be read from the PDF)' and log moisture and contamination as measured percentages on the processing record, with the buyer's deduction as an editable rule per buyer. Payment terms must include: GST reverse charge when a yard sells metal scrap without a GSTIN (buyer self-invoices within 30 days), 2% GST TDS on metal-scrap contracts over Rs 2.5 lakh between registered parties, and income-tax TCS on scrap (2% from 1 Apr 2026 as proposed; confirm enacted rate) — all stored as dated admin-editable rules per the repo's legal research. Price levels: record every trade with its material state so that L3 = the price a pre-processor or recycler pays a yard for S3 bales/lots, L4 = the price a recycler or compounder charges a manufacturer for S7/S8 feedstock, and a pre-processor's flake/crumb/aggregate sale to a recycler is tagged by state (S4-S6) rather than forced into L3 or L4; each processing record then stores yield, by-product lots and residual lots with their own price or disposal cost. Status stays 'needs-pilot-or-counsel'; the ten-phone-call plan in Peenya and Bommasandra stands, adding a question on how each buyer applies GST RCM/TDS and TCS to the quoted price.
